title: introduce-credential-warmup-adapter-and-async-iterator-harmonizer-for-py-ts-go
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Teams reported a recurring cold-start cost when the SDK rotated credentials under bursty streaming load. This PR introduces a small, transport-agnostic 'credential warmup adapter' that prefetches / primes credentials before the first heavy streaming usage and a light 'async iterator harmonizer' that normalizes buffer/backoff signals across Python/TS/Go SDKs. The goals are: (1) remove auth handshake stalls that surface as first-request tail latency, (2) provide a single opt-in knob for credential warmup and backpressure hints across SDKS, and (3) align telemetry labels so we can correlate warmup success with reduced token spend.

What this PR does (summary): single continuous description string covering change areas and checklist. - Add credential warmup adapter implementations in py/ts/go (small, opt-in component). - Introduce an 'iterator harmonizer' helper that standardizes pause/resume/backoff event contracts for async iterables/generators across languages. - Wire metrics (sdk.auth.warmup.*, sdk.iter.harmonizer.*) and a lightweight end-to-end smoke test per SDK. - Bump package minor versions: py 1.31.0, ts 1.28.3, go 1.9.2 to pick up shape changes in the iterator helpers. - Docs: add migration note, usage examples for enabling warmup and a troubleshooting FAQ. - Add changelog entries and compatibility note (non-breaking opt-in only).

Checklist: - [x] Implementation for Python - [x] Implementation for TypeScript - [x] Implementation for Go - [x] Unit tests for adapters - [x] SDK smoke e2e tests for warmup under mocked control plane - [x] Docs & changelog - [x] Version bumps and release notes

Notes: This is intentionally opt-in: default behavior unchanged. The adapter exposes a small interface (enable_warmup / warmup_timeout_ms / prefetch_count) documented per SDK. The harmonizer attempts to be conservative in producer/consumer semantics to avoid surprising changes to existing iterables. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes were introduced. Linked Linear items track telemetry dashboards and perf checklists.

release_notes:
- SDKs: Introduce optional credential warmup adapter to reduce first-request tail latency under credential rotation scenarios.
- SDKs: Add async iterator harmonizer that standardizes pause/resume/backoff signals across Python/TypeScript/Go.
- Telemetry: new metrics sdk.auth.warmup.* and sdk.iter.harmonizer.* and label sdk.auth.warmup.credential_source.
- Non-breaking, opt-in. See docs/sdk/warmup.md and migration notes for examples and knobs.
notes_for_release_team: Recommend enabling the warmup adapter behind a feature flag for one week in canary customers. Monitor sdk.auth.warmup.success_rate and request tail p95 for first-token requests. No mandatory action for existing customers.
